title.value: SmOOD: Smoothness-based Out-of-Distribution Detection Approach for Surrogate Neural Networks in Aircraft Design
title.justification: The exact title from the paper was chosen as it captures the main focus of the study.
title.quote: SmOOD: Smoothness-based Out-of-Distribution Detection Approach for Surrogate Neural Networks in Aircraft Design

extractions.description: This paper introduces SmOOD, a smoothness-based approach to Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection for surrogate neural networks used in aircraft design. The approach seeks to improve the accuracy and reliability of surrogate models, such as feedforward neural networks (FNNs), by detecting OOD inputs and routing high-risk predictions to high-fidelity (HF) models for validation. This is expected to enhance the efficiency and reliability of aircraft design optimizations by utilizing the smoothness properties of the HF simulations.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on developing a method to improve aircraft design processes through surrogate modeling and OOD detection. Although efficiency improvements can indirectly benefit environmental concerns by reducing resource consumption, climate change is not a central theme of the study.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Aircraft industry is constantly striving for more efficient design optimization methods in terms of human efforts, computation time, and resources consumption.

primary_category.justification: This paper is focused on surrogate modeling for aircraft design and OOD detection, which does not directly align with any listed primary climate change categories such as mitigation, adaptation, etc.
primary_category.quote: Through SmOOD, our smoothness-based out-of-distribution detection approach, we propose to code-sign a model-dependent OOD indicator with the optimized FNN surrogate, to produce a trustworthy surrogate model with selective but credible predictions.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper doesn't address related climate change categories or sub-categories beyond its primary focus on aircraft design optimization using surrogate models and OOD detection.
secondary_categories.quote: The next step will be to develop an active version of SmOOD that stores the revealed OODs to fine-tune the FNN and expand further the ID regions, which results in fewer requests to the HF model and faster design assessments.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, or other climate-related themes are not discussed in this paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: SmOOD, a smoothness-based OOD detection strategy, ensures selective and reliable predictions on the ID inputs that are identified by their proximity to smooth domain regions.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper's focus on aircraft design and surrogate model optimization does not correspond to any of the specific sub-categories listed.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Results show that FNN-based surrogates outperform their Gaussian Process counterparts in terms of predictive performance.

applications.justification: The study is applied to improving the efficiency and reliability of surrogate models in aircraft design, which involves optimizing aircraft performance factors using machine learning techniques.
applications.quote: Hybrid surrogate optimization maintains high results quality while providing rapid design assessments when both the surrogate model and the switch mechanism for eventually transitioning to the HF model are calibrated properly.

new_primary_category.justification: This new category is proposed because the content of the paper centers around optimizing aircraft design processes using surrogate models and OOD detection, which is distinct from the provided climate change categories.
new_primary_category.quote: The design of aircraft, from conceptualization to commercialization, is expensive. Their lead-time engineering process can take many years and cost billions of dollars from design to manufacture.

new_primary_sub_category.value: Surrogate Modeling and OOD Detection in Aerospace
new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper focuses on surrogate modeling and out-of-distribution detection tailored specifically for aerospace engineering, hence a new sub-category is suggested.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: SmOOD exploits inherent smoothness properties of the HF simulations to effectively expose OODs through revealing their suspicious sensitivities, thereby avoiding over-confident uncertainty estimates on OOD samples.
